old: - **Robot-vacuum sensors.** A *laser distance sensor* (LDS) is the small spinning turret on a robot vacuum, which maps the room in a 2D plane. *Triangulation* LDS units view the laser spot with an offset detector and infer distance from the spot's position; dToF units time the echo instead. *SLAM* (simultaneous localization and mapping) builds a map while tracking the robot in it; *VSLAM* does so from camera images.
new: - **Robot-vacuum sensors.** A *laser distance sensor* (LDS) is the small spinning turret on a robot vacuum, which maps the room in a 2D plane. *Triangulation* LDS units view the laser spot with an offset detector and infer distance from the spot's position; Camsense's D series pairs a VCSEL with a CMOS image sensor for this. *dToF* LDS units time each laser pulse's round trip instead: LDROBOT's filings define dToF this way, and Camsense's P series pairs a VCSEL with a SPAD receiver [P]. Both kinds are motor-driven 360° scanners, so the housing does not show which principle is inside; LDROBOT's Series 26 and Camsense's PXA are dToF units built to replace a triangulation unit without changes to the robot [P]. *SLAM* (simultaneous localization and mapping) builds a map while tracking the robot in it; *VSLAM* does so from camera images.

old: - **Verification of dToF, 3 Oct 2026.** LDROBOT's Apr 2026 prospectus defines DTOF as directly measuring laser-pulse travel time (p. 28), and describes the Mini DTOF Series 06 as a 360° scanning pulse-timing sensor (pp. 134–135). Its Aug 2026 interim results explicitly report more than 4 M DTOF lidar shipments in 2025 (p. 3). Camsense likewise describes its P-series dTOF products as VCSEL + SPAD sensors (p. 150). These disclosures support **dToF** for the named product categories; no iToF substitution is warranted. Mechanical scanning and external shape do not identify the ranging principle: LDROBOT's Series 26 is a dToF sensor with a triangular shape intended to replace triangulation units. Its shipment count covers the company's robotics sensor business and does not establish how many units went into robot vacuums alone.
